title: Diosgenin exerts dual impacts on Th17 cell differentiation in adjuvant-induced arthritis rats by impairing SIRT1-mediated deacetylation.
authors: Yin, Qin; Zhai, Yu-Ting; Jin, Hong-Rui; Yang, Kui; Wu, Yi-Jin; Sun, Han-Fei; Zuo, Jian
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨薯蓣皂苷通过抑制SIRT1去乙酰化影响Th17分化及关节炎治疗，虽涉及分子模拟但核心为细胞信号通路与疾病机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dioscorea spongiosa is used in China as the herbal medicine Bixie. PURPOSE: This study investigated how SIRT1-inhibitory effects affect its therapeutic outcomes in adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA). METHODS: AIA rats were treated with the extract of D. spongiosa (BX), diosgenin, or together with an NF-kappaB inhibitor. Therapeutic effects were assessed by ELISA, flow cytometry, and histology analyses. Affinities of compounds to SIRT1 were evaluated based on molecular simulation, immunoprecipitation, spectroscopy, protein stability, and isothermal titration calorimetry data. SIRT1 and NF-kappaB signals were regulated by siRNA, overexpression plasmids, and inhibitors. Pathway status was characterized by PCR, WB, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and reporter gene assays. RESULTS: BX ameliorated joint damage and inflammation in AIA rats. These effects weakened with increasing doses. This therapy upregulated acetylation in the spleen. Diosgenin, a major compound in BX bioactive fraction, exhibited distinct effects on IL-17A release at varied concentrations, which was identified as a SIRT1 inhibitor subsequently. In Jurkat T cells, diosgenin impaired deacetylation, exerting different impacts on the transcriptional activities of p65 NF-kappaB and RORgammat. The effects were antagonized by SIRT1 overexpression, and abolished when SIRT1 was silenced. In the presence of NF-kappaB inhibitors, diosgenin reduced IL-17A secretion of Jurkat cells in a concentration-dependent manner, and its therapeutic effects on AIA were further enhanced. CONCLUSION: Diosgenin-mediated impairment of deacetylation benefited AIA rats by inhibiting RORgammat activity. However, at high concentrations, this SIRT1-inhibitory effect promoted Th17 differentiation via NF-kappaB activation. These findings provide a theoretical basis for optimizing Bixie-relevant therapies, and highlight potential risks of SIRT1-targeted therapies.
abstract_zh: 背景：薯蓣（Dioscorea spongiosa）在中国被用作草药萆薢。目的：本研究探讨SIRT1抑制效应如何影响其在佐剂诱导性关节炎（AIA）中的治疗效果。方法：AIA大鼠分别接受薯蓣提取物（BX）、薯蓣皂苷元（diosgenin）治疗，或与NF-kappaB抑制剂联合使用。通过ELISA、流式细胞术和组织学分析评估治疗效果。基于分子模拟、免疫沉淀、光谱学、蛋白质稳定性和等温滴定量热法数据，评估化合物对SIRT1的亲和力。通过siRNA、过表达质粒和抑制剂调控SIRT1和NF-kappaB信号。通过PCR、WB、免疫组织化学、免疫荧光和报告基因实验表征通路状态。结果：BX改善了AIA大鼠的关节损伤和炎症。这些效应随剂量增加而减弱。该治疗上调了脾脏中的乙酰化水平。薯蓣皂苷元是BX生物活性组分中的主要化合物，在不同浓度下对IL-17A释放表现出不同效应，随后被鉴定为SIRT1抑制剂。在Jurkat T细胞中，薯蓣皂苷元损害去乙酰化作用，对p65 NF-kappaB和RORgammat的转录活性产生不同影响。这些效应被SIRT1过表达所拮抗，并在SIRT1沉默时被消除。在NF-kappaB抑制剂存在下，薯蓣皂苷元以浓度依赖性方式减少Jurkat细胞的IL-17A分泌，其对AIA的治疗效果进一步增强。结论：薯蓣皂苷元介导的去乙酰化损害通过抑制RORgammat活性使AIA大鼠受益。然而，在高浓度下，这种SIRT1抑制效应通过NF-kappaB激活促进Th17分化。这些发现为优化萆薢相关疗法提供了理论基础，并强调了SIRT1靶向治疗的潜在风险。
